id="ADR-0002" title="Use OPA (embedded) for scope policy evaluation" status="Proposed" inferred=false
author="Donald Gifford" created="2026-05-10"
summary=""
context="The Agent Capability Tokens RFC (RFC-NNNN) requires a policy engine to evaluate capability…"
decision="Use **Open Policy Agent (OPA) embedded as a Go library** via `github.com/open-policy-agent…"
consequences positive=5 negative=4 neutral=3
alternatives=0 open-questions=0 references=8

positive line=114
  text="**Single policy language across IaC, K8s admission, agent capability, and egress.** One Rego skill set serves four use cases."

positive line=116
  text="**No new daemon to operate.** Embedded library; if the agent runs, the policy engine runs."

positive line=118
  text="**Decision Logs feature gives free audit trail.** OPA can emit every evaluation as a structured log; ties cleanly into Langfuse / OTel."

positive line=120
  text="**regal lint** catches Rego anti-patterns in CI; the language is notorious for spaghetti without discipline, and the linter is the discipline."

positive line=122
  text="**Familiar idiom.** OPA's `data.<package>.allow` and `input.<...>` patterns are widely documented; new engineers ramp in days."

negative line=129
  text="**Rego is its own language.** New hires unfamiliar with it pay a learning cost. Mitigated by the existing Conftest usage — several team members already know Rego."

negative line=132
  text="**Cedar's IAM-shape syntax is genuinely nicer for our specific use case.** Cedar's `permit(principal, action, resource)` reads more naturally for capability authz than Rego's general-purpose data structure. Accepted cost; consistency wins."

negative line=136
  text="**OPA bundle size.** The embedded evaluator adds ~5MB to the framework binary. Not a meaningful cost in a containerized deployment."

negative line=138
  text="**Policy debugging requires Rego comfort.** `opa eval --explain` is excellent but assumes Rego literacy. Cedar has similar tooling but with a more approachable language. Net wash given the consistency benefit."

neutral line=146
  text="**Both OPA and Cedar are OSS, both have Go SDKs.** Licensing and language-support concerns are equivalent."

neutral line=148
  text="**Both evaluate in microseconds.** Performance is not the deciding factor."

neutral line=149
  text="**Both are likely to remain healthy projects.** OPA is CNCF graduated; Cedar is AWS-backed with growing community adoption. Neither is a survival risk."

reference line=205 url=""
  text="Sibling: RFC-NNNN Agent Capability Tokens — uses this engine"

reference line=206 url=""
  text="Sibling: ADR-NNNN Use JWT for v1 — produces the claims this engine evaluates"

reference line=207 url=""
  text="Internal: Existing Conftest-for-Terraform-IaC usage in homelab Kubernetes security stack — same Rego skill set"
